column8: Mon 16 Nov: 3c, the RBA's guidance was conditional in its own words (at the earliest, sustainably within the target), which aha A needs beside row 2; the RBA earns its place on the record, never as a nod to the team's home.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c, why nothing is stated before the move: the case's warning on overpromising, lived by a central bank in its own review (quote checked at source today); on merit the cleanest documented case of a forecast heard as a promise and broken, so no mention of the team's home.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d, co-sponsors carry away the figure and drop its condition (both quotes checked at source today); the top keeps its one cost exception where SKELETON 3d carries it, so say no caveat about whether the money exists, not no caveat at all.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c, the RBA's own summary that mixing a condition and a date gets only the date heard; the cited papers (Feroli et al. 2017, Broadbent 2022) are unread, so cite the RBA only.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c and Table 2, a number given as an example became the anchor; fix the use: SKELETON 3d names $95,000 as the figure co-sponsors count, so say 3d carries only the two owned ends and no modelled or example figure, never that 3d holds no figure.

Mon 16 Nov: store only: the RBA broke on the upside, but giving more than a stated top breaks nothing for Laura (Q25-001), so the cap is not what protects her; the parallel breaks under its own disanalogy.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c, both reviews name the long horizon as the fault, which is aha 7's speaking early; figures match NUMBERS 4 (10.7% at 12 months); reword per AHA row 7: a top named early would turn out larger than the move could buy, never not yet owned.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c, aha B: central banks cured it by saying less (quotes checked at source today; the no-published-path line is in the review's overview, not section 4); Laura cannot, since the case asks for a dollar range, so she owns first and speaks second.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d, the listeners who act on a figure are the ones who hear a promise; never say the guidance caused the fixed-rate borrowing, which the RBA also ties to low fixed rates and its funding scheme.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d colour beside row 2: the speaker meant a condition, the listeners heard a promise; one interview by a governor defending his bank, so one clause at most.
Mon 16 Nov: background only (0.10% to 3.10% in seven months, Keel arithmetic on the RBA table); adds nothing beyond rows 2-3, store only.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d's plainest line (the community did not hear the conditionality) rests on news reports; read the Senate Hansard of 28 Nov 2022 before any use, and drop the ABC's loan count.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d and 3e, a broken commitment taxes the next one; for Laura the next ask is the yearly programme money from 2033 (SKELETON 3d), which makes the Keel inference concrete.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: the yield-target lessons (short enough for very high confidence; a fixed maturity) repeat row 7's horizon point, and the RBA defended a market price, not owned money.
Mon 16 Nov: twin of Q7c-004 (Stanford's exit named after the fall) as the contrast with IPS l.17's two reasons named in advance; Q7c-004 is closer to Laura's kind of rule.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c and 3d, the arm's-length review heard a broken promise and blamed reliance on detailed caveats, which is what makes the RBA the best case (claim 4); its glossary's a commitment is one clause at most; the top's cost exception stays where 3d carries it.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c, aha C: an early figure bent the speaker's own forecasts; keep may have, and note Laura's top comes from a written rule, so the pressure would fall on keeping the move to half (IPS l.15), not on the arithmetic.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: a board's governance lesson (guidance is a policy decision); Laura decides alone and her figure is NUMBERS 4's rule output, which 3c already says.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: the Fed's three dates; the asymmetry they are used for is Q71-005's, and the extensions were deliberate easing, so the episode does not show it.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d, Raskin: date guidance moved expectations because it was taken as firm; a figure meant to move co-sponsors to pledge will be taken as firm, so it must be; market evidence, not donors.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c, aha D: the risk was written down on the first day by one FOMC member (minutes checked at source today; three dissents preferring extended period); a US source a Wharton judge can place, and the one Fed line row 40 pairs with the RBA.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c, a not-a-promise label works for a judge, not a co-sponsor; Bernanke's line was about the projections, so lead with the minutes' line on the guidance and Woodford (row 27) for how it was heard.
Mon 16 Nov: vocabulary only (Delphic means a forecast); adds nothing unless 3c names the two kinds, and then one word beside row 24.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c vocabulary: without a rope central banks rely on reputation, Laura on what she owns; the rope image competes with pencil and ink and Q7's rule on Elster (never the image), and Laura could still sell, so never rope already tied.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: markets read the dates as forecasts while the press heard promises; row 33 does the qualifier's job better; the discussant's name is unchecked.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: both readings coexisted among forecasters (read in excerpts, not in full); the co-sponsor split it implies is Keel inference.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c, Woodford: an unusual statement invites the strongest reading, and a three-year unconditional commitment is unwise unless the money is owned; he argues for better commitment, not against it.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c, theory's form of Laura's order, act then speak (Bassetto: actions speak louder than words); fix the judge's note: IPS l.15 calls the bottom what she can promise, so never she does not promise; say her promise reports money already owned, held for her and shown on request.
Mon 16 Nov: a 27 Nov check for 3d's sentence (a commitment, clear, read as meant); the feature's authors are unchecked and needed for APA before citing.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c or Table 2's note, the Bank of England's forecast became the date people remembered (So there was a date? No, there was a forecast.); supports modelled figures for the judge and owned ones for co-sponsors; a second case after the RBA only if room.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d's test, would a co-sponsor need to read a caveat; a committee's worry, not a measured result; the plan's answer holds outright for the bottom and for the top with its one cost exception.
Mon 16 Nov: twin of Q94-008, the same lesson (central banks kept freedom by saying less; Laura must name dollars, so she owns them first); the ECB quotes stay findable in the store.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c, the honest qualifier: a caveat can be taught by years of repetition (Riksbank), with Posen's early counterpoint; Laura has one meeting per co-sponsor, which is why claim 3 says the people who budget on it.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c and 3d, the mechanism from the psychology of reasoning: a conditional about the speaker's own action is heard as a promise; it bridges central banks to Laura, whose contribution is her own act; Evans read in abstract only.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: lab result that vague words move no one; the case already asks for a dollar range, so the report needs no argument for precision; abstract only.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: Nordic banks in 2025-26 still treat it as a live risk; more of row 2's point, and the 2026 lecture's speaker is unchecked.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: the one short, explicit promise that held (RBNZ, 12 months); Laura's runs about two years, and the RBNZ's held partly because the economy allowed it, so the parallel is loose.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c's reason in notes (heard as a promise by the people who budget on it); fix before use: the principle's one home is 3.0 (AHA row 4), so 3c gives only the reason; each end rounded down risks the banned reading of rounding the parts (SKELETON 3c, H2: the top's sum is rounded once); a top named early would turn out larger than the move could buy, never not yet owned (AHA row 7).

Mon 16 Nov: 3c conceit candidate (the RBA's pencil figure read as ink; Laura writes only in ink); 3c already has let the ink dry and V2 allows one turn per part, so test it cold against that turn; never in tables or Laura's words.

Mon 16 Nov: the choice of example, on merit: only the RBA has both its own and an independent review finding a forecast heard as a promise and broken; the RBA plus one Fed line (row 21); never the team's home beside it.
